prompt: In today’s world, it is no longer necessary to attend live performances such as shows or concerts, as watching them on television or on a computer at home is considered a better option. Do you agree or disagree with this opinion?
essay:
Some people question the necessity of attending live performances when watching them at home on television is said to be a better alternative. While I understand the appeal of watching plays, concerts, and other events from the comfort of home, I ultimately disagree that this is superior to experiencing them in person.

It is easy to see why many people prefer watching performances on television. One obvious benefit is that people can avoid travelling, paying high ticket prices, and dealing with large crowds. Viewers also have the option to pause, rewind, or replay parts of the show as desired, which would not be possible in a live setting. In addition, television broadcasts often use multiple camera angles and professional editing to highlight details that may be difficult to see from a distance in a theatre or concert hall. With modern recording technology, high-definition visuals and high-quality sound can further enhance the viewing experience.

However, these benefits do not outweigh what is lost when a performance is not experienced live. The most important difference is the atmosphere created in the venue itself. Being surrounded by a live audience produces a sense of shared excitement through applause, laughter, and spontaneous reactions, which cannot be replicated through a screen. Live performances also feel more engaging because they are unpredictable. Small mistakes, improvisations, or unexpected audience interactions make each show unique and memorable. Once aired on television, these moments are often refined or removed altogether, which can result in a significantly less authentic performance.

In conclusion, although watching performances at home is undeniably convenient and sometimes visually impressive, it cannot replace the emotional intensity and uniqueness of attending a live event. For this reason, I believe live performances remain the more valuable experience.
